scope: Purposively selected published arguments about political learning; not a roster of activists, a prevalence sample, or an operational network.
analysis_status: Single AI-assisted interpretive pass. Source passages inspected; no independent coding, author verification, interviews, behavioral verification, or causal estimation.
counting_rule: Ten records come from six receiving documents. Multiple records in one document are dependent; these counts describe the register, not a population.
privacy_rule: Retain only public publication names and source locators. Do not resolve pseudonyms, infer private affiliations, or extract operational activities.

sources.author: Anonymous contributor introduced by CrimethInc. as an anarchist
sources.title: Ya Ghazze Habibti—Gaza, My Love: Understanding the Genocide in Palestine
sources.access: Publisher HTML; framing, Serafinski passage, and reading list inspected. Other historical, legal, and strategic claims were not audited.

observations.referenced_source: Nihilist arguments assembled in the pamphlet; not a single externally identified teacher
observations.retrieval_anchor: my evaluation of this subject material comes from an anarchist orientation
observations.observed: The writer explicitly situates the evaluation within anarchism while introducing nihilist contributions to other anarchists.
observations.limit: Reader reception and behavioral adoption are not demonstrated by the invitation.

observations.referenced_source: Bæden and an unnamed-in-this-passage Warsaw Ghetto memoir
observations.locator: Collision, paragraph beginning This collision of anarcho-nihilism
observations.retrieval_anchor: At the same time as I pored my way through Bæden
observations.observed: The author reports simultaneous reading as the origin of the juxtaposition developed in the book.
observations.limit: Do not identify the unnamed memoir from another citation without additional evidence. The report does not verify the book's historical analogy.

observations.locator: Anarcho-nihilism, paragraph beginning In short and following attribution
observations.retrieval_anchor: Aragorn! traces the history of nihilism
observations.observed: The text explicitly uses Aragorn! in constructing its account.
observations.limit: This verifies attributed use, not the historical accuracy of that account, independent behavioral uptake, or another recipient.

observations.referenced_source: John Zerzan's writing and Why Hope?
observations.locator: Opening paragraph; subsequent response to the quoted essay
observations.retrieval_anchor: For years, John Zerzan has inspired my understanding
observations.observed: The writer credits an existing influence while disputing the essay's interpretation of nihilism.
observations.limit: Influence and disagreement coexist; this is not evidence of either total deference or complete disaffiliation.

observations.referenced_source: Unspecified nihilist, individualist anarchists named as a category by the author
observations.locator: Paragraph beginning During the conclusion of my participation
observations.retrieval_anchor: inspired me to see anarchy in an entirely different way
observations.observed: The author attributes a change of understanding following an organizing impasse to this source category.
observations.limit: No specific people, exact encounter date, exclusive cause, or verified later practice can be inferred.

observations.locator: Passage introduced In response to this I would like to share a quote and attributed to the book
observations.observed: An attributed excerpt is used to support the reply's argument.
observations.limit: Textual reuse is not independent verification of the quotation's claims or of enacted practice.

observations.locator: First response paragraph after Zerzan's opening discussion of Desert
observations.observed: The responding author explicitly states they have not read this text.
observations.limit: Bounded to the time of the statement. Secondhand exposure through Zerzan remains possible; do not code absence of all influence.

observations.referenced_source: Max Stirner, The Ego and its Own
observations.retrieval_anchor: I recommend Stirner's The Ego and its Own
observations.observed: A selective recommendation appears within a critical discussion of egoism and nihilism.
observations.limit: Stirner is not automatically a nihilist or an insurrectionary in the study's classification; this record tests stance separation, not the target category's prevalence.

observations.referenced_source: Insurrectionalist arguments, including Bonanno texts identified in the source notes
observations.locator: The ideas of insurrectionalism; Waiting for the revolution?; Critique of organisation; numbered notes naming The Anarchist Tension and Armed Joy
observations.observed: The article quotes and disputes organizational and strategic arguments, with some partial agreements.
evidence_basis: observable argumentative engagement with attributed texts
observations.limit: No new organizational practice is shown to result. Do not substitute The Insurrectional Project for the different Bonanno works actually cited.

observations.referenced_source: Serafinski, Blessed is the Flame, S22
observations.locator: Paragraph beginning One last note before we move forward; concluding reading list
observations.observed: The contributor explicitly brings the book's argument into a different political interpretation.
observations.limit: Publication is not proof of all CrimethInc. contributors' agreement, audience uptake, historical equivalence, or practical efficacy. Analysis does not endorse violence against civilians.

interpretation_boundaries: A document's stance toward a source and its learning from that source are separate variables.
The register establishes textual relations and reported learning episodes, not a representative gradient.
No inspected record independently verifies subsequent enactment of a specific practice.
The evidence selection followed references and theoretical contrasts, so source prominence within this register cannot estimate prominence outside it.
Retrieval anchors are brief locators; typographic apostrophes may differ across archived editions.
All source access for this register occurred during the second revision round on 2026-10-15; this does not certify the first edition's claimed search history.
